paras_en: On Friday, November 7, 2026 (reporting by You Analysis/Industry Data Center), U.S. markets closed mixed. After a sharp drop the day before, technology stocks rebounded, led by chip stocks, pushing the Nasdaq index up 1.1%. The S&P 500 edged higher, while the Dow Jones continued to fall. The tech rally was not enough to reverse the week’s overall weakness, and the Nasdaq recorded its fourth straight week of declines as the market kept weighing AI investment prospects against interest‑rate direction.

The Nasdaq finished up 264 points at 24,579, a 1.1% gain; the S&P 500 rose 23 points to 7,377, up 0.32%; and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 237 points to 51,286, down 0.46%. Over the full week the Nasdaq slipped 3.4%, the S&P 500 fell 2.7%, and the Dow dropped 0.9%, with the S&P 500 delivering its worst weekly performance in more than a year.

Semiconductor stocks led the rebound, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumping 4.2%. Nvidia (NVDA-US) rose 2.8%, AMD (AMD-US) surged 11%, and memory‑chip maker SanDisk (SNDK-US) recovered nearly 4%. After a strong opening, tech stocks held most of their gains; the Nasdaq was up about 2% mid‑session before narrowing its advance at the close. S&P 500 sectors diverged, with information technology leading gains while consumer staples and health care lagged.

Better‑than‑expected employment data lifted bets on further Fed rate hikes. October non‑farm payrolls exceeded forecasts and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, indicating a still‑resilient labor market. LSEG data show traders now see a 78% probability of a December rate increase, up from 70% earlier, making rate expectations another focal point beyond the tech rebound.

On the stock‑specific front, Tesla (TSLA-US) climbed 4.2%, rebounding from the prior day’s decline. Enterprise‑software firm Atlassian (TEAM-US) saw its shares plunge 16% after releasing its Q1 earnings. Short‑term rental platform Airbnb (ABNB-US) lifted its 2026 full‑year revenue growth outlook, sending the stock up 12% and highlighting the stark performance split among individual equities.

The recent volatility has pulled the Nasdaq about 10% lower from its peak a month ago, placing it in correction territory, and Friday’s bounce did not recover the losses incurred earlier in the week. Energy stocks also felt pressure, with the S&P 500 energy sector index down 12% for the week, marking its worst weekly performance since April 2025.

paras_en: If AI stocks keep falling, will the Fed still raise rates? The “Fed mouthpiece” points to a December key point. The Wall Street Journal’s Nick Timiraos wrote on Friday (the 6th) that whether the Federal Reserve raises rates again in December may be less important than the current correction in AI stocks, which could be more significant than the just‑released non‑farm payroll data. Recent economic data and officials’ comments still point to another rate hike in December, but if AI‑stock selling pressure persists and drags down consumer spending and corporate investment, the financial markets themselves could produce part of the tightening effect that a rate hike is meant to achieve.

Fed’s Mary Daly: Despite tech‑stock plunge, the Fed may still raise rates. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said on Friday (the 6th) that the Federal Reserve is likely still required to raise rates further to bring down persistently high inflation, though the timing and magnitude remain uncertain. Even though tech stocks have recently undergone a painful re‑pricing, she believes policymakers must judge based on the overall economic situation and adopt a cautious, incremental policy‑adjustment path in a highly uncertain environment.

TSMC may venture into AI memory? Reports say Nvidia has asked it to develop 3D DRAM. Foreign media citing The Information on Friday (the 7th) reported that at the request of its biggest customer Nvidia (NVDA‑US), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (2330‑TW) (TSM‑US) has begun working on a 3D DRAM production plan. Insiders say TSMC is evaluating two options: building a new fab or acquiring an existing plant and converting it into a memory production line. The plan is still in the study phase and a production timeline has not been set.

Which Nvidia AI chips can still be sold to China? The US may set a “two‑generation lag” threshold. Bloomberg reported on Friday (the 6th) that bipartisan members of Congress are negotiating a proposal to keep the current AI‑chip export restrictions in place for 18 months, during which China would only be able to obtain technology that is at least two generations behind the United States’ most advanced products. Nvidia’s H200, which has already been approved for sale to China, is exactly two generations behind the latest Rubin series. After Democrats take control of Congress in January next year, CEO Jensen Huang may face another issue: how Nvidia can verify that chips sold to overseas customers ultimately do not get shipped to China.

items.title: AI反成利多!！Airbnb自造AI旅遊助理 一站式規劃旅程 客服成本年減17%
items.title_en: AI Turns Into a Boost! Airbnb Builds Its Own AI Travel Assistant for One‑Stop Trip Planning, Cutting Customer Service Costs by 17% Annually
paras: Airbnb重返成長軌道，第三季營收、訂房金額及獲利均優於市場預期，執行長Brian Chesky更宣布將打造自家的AI旅遊代理，預計2027年上半年開始向房客推出。市場看好財報表現及成長展望，Airbnb (ABNB-US)股價周五(6日)收盤大漲11.67%，報189.99美元。
Airbnb周四(5日)公布第三季財報，營收年增19%至48.7億美元，高於分析師預估的47.4億美元，並創下逾三年來最快增速；每股盈餘3.16美元，也高於市場預估的2.85美元。總訂房金額(GBV)年增21%至277億美元，淨利達19億美元，調整後EBITDA年增22%至25億美元，利潤率達52%。
營運數據同樣強勁，第三季住宿晚數與體驗預訂量合計達1.55億筆，年增16%；平均每日房價(ADR)年增4%，若排除匯率影響則成長5%。公司指出，全球各區域住宿晚數均實現雙位數成長，北美訂房量更創四年來最快增速，首次預訂用戶年增13%，為2022年初以來最高，且以Z世代成長最快。
各地市場也呈現加速趨勢。法國、英國、加拿大、澳洲及美國五大核心市場均較前季加快，拉丁美洲與亞太地區訂房晚數年增逾20%，歐洲、中東及非洲(EMEA)成長中段雙位數；巴西成長逾30%，印度逾60%，日本則達低20%區間。此外，透過手機App完成的住宿晚數年增29%，占總訂房量66%。
Airbnb表示，這波成長並非由單一產品帶動，而是多年來改善平台技術、營運流程及產品體驗的成果。公司第三季推出逾50項產品與功能，較去年同期增加近70%，AI加速產品開發與測試，讓公司能更快推出新服務。
AI也開始直接改善營運效率。Airbnb的AI客服助理目前支援逾50種語言，第三季約40%的所有客服問題無須人工介入即可解決，高於第二季約三分之一；每筆訂單的客服成本也年減逾17%。公司並正將AI客服擴展至美國語音服務，讓房客與房東能透過電話取得協助。
不過，Airbnb下一步並不只把AI用於客服，而是希望打造專門處理旅遊需求的自家AI代理。Chesky在法說會上表示，公司不認為傳統聊天機器人適合規劃旅行，也不認為消費者會用單一AI代理處理所有事情，因為旅行本身具有探索與期待的特性，選擇目的地、瀏覽住宿及比較選項，也是旅程體驗的一部分。
Chesky指出，約80%的旅客享受研究旅行的過程；Airbnb內部數據則顯示，超過75%的房客在選擇住宿時會使用平台地圖，逾90%會瀏覽多張房源照片，70%會在預訂前閱讀評論，平均每筆訂單約有3名旅客，因此住宿選擇往往需要同行者共同決定。
Airbnb自家AI代理將採用生成式介面(Generative UI)，而非只提供文字對話。系統可從數百種旅遊專用介面元件中，即時組合地圖、照片、比較表、日曆及行程表，依照房客需求提供合適的操作介面，並讓使用者直接在Airbnb內探索、比較及完成預訂。
公司認為，自家代理具備外部通用型AI工具難以複製的優勢，包括近20年累積的房東與房客市場資料，以及平台本身掌握訂單、付款和客服流程。這意味著AI代理未來不只能協助搜尋住宿，也可處理更改訂單、付款問題、退款、重新預訂及旅途中安全支援等需求。Airbnb計畫2027年上半年開始向房客推出，並逐步整合住宿、飯店、服務及體驗等旅遊項目。
除了AI，Airbnb也積極擴大住宿以外的業務。公司目前已在全球逾60個主要目的地提供數千家精品及獨立飯店，飯店預訂成長速度明顯快於核心住宿業務；約35%首次透過Airbnb預訂飯店的旅客，會在一年內回頭預訂平台上的房源。公司也陸續推出租車、餐點配送、洗衣、嬰兒用品、滑雪裝備及船隻租賃等服務。
合作通路方面，Airbnb於10月與美國運通 (American Express) (AXP-US) 啟動獨家合作，將超過100萬筆Airbnb房源導入Amex Travel。管理層表示，合作初期已帶來數千筆訂單，其中近四分之一來自首次使用Airbnb的旅客，有助於擴大客源並吸引較高端的旅遊客群。
財務方面，Airbnb第三季自由現金流達14億美元，過去12個月累計49億美元，自由現金流利潤率為35%。公司當季回購7億美元股票，原有回購授權尚餘27億美元，董事會另批准新增最多120億美元股票回購額度，反映管理層對現金流及未來成長的信心。
公司也持續調整收費制度，10月完成最後階段的費率簡化，幾乎所有房東都已轉入單一15.5%服務費制度。第三季隱含抽成率為17.6%，略低於去年同期，主要受到「立即預訂、稍後付款」(Reserve Now, Pay Later)方案影響，因為旅客提前預訂推高總訂房金額，但相關收入尚未同步認列。
該付款方案也帶動第三季住宿晚數與體驗預訂量增加約3個百分點，若排除這項影響，年增率仍約13%，較第二季加快。不過，彈性付款及較長的提前預訂時間，也使取消率由去年同期的16%升至19%，管理層表示，整體取消率較去年增加約200至300個基點，後續仍將觀察相關變化。
展望第四季，Airbnb預估營收介於32.2億至32.8億美元，年增16%至18%，其中包含約2個百分點的匯率順風；總訂房金額預估年增中段雙位數，住宿晚數與體驗預訂量至少成長低雙位數。公司預期第四季調整後EBITDA將高於去年同期，但利潤率可能略降，部分受到行銷支出認列時點影響。
Airbnb同時上調2026年全年展望，預估營收年增率將達高段十幾個百分點，高於先前至少中段十幾個百分點的預測；全年調整後EBITDA利潤率目標也由至少35.5%提高至約36%。
Chesky表示，對Airbnb這種規模的平台而言，重新加速成長並不常見，而公司目前正處於這個階段。從財報來看，訂房需求回溫、首次使用者增加及AI客服降本，已共同推升營運表現；接下來市場關注的重點，將是自家AI代理能否進一步提高轉換率、擴大旅遊服務收入，並讓Airbnb從住宿預訂平台發展為一站式旅遊服務入口。
paras_en: Airbnb is back on a growth trajectory, with third‑quarter revenue, booking value and profit all beating market expectations. CEO Brian Chesky also announced the creation of its own AI travel agent, slated to roll out to guests in the first half of 2027. The market welcomed the earnings and outlook, sending Airbnb (ABNB‑US) shares up 11.67% on Friday the 6th to close at $189.99.

Airbnb reported third‑quarter results on Thursday the 5th, showing revenue up 19% year‑over‑year to $4.87 billion, above analysts’ estimate of $4.74 billion and the fastest pace in more than three years. Diluted earnings were $3.16 per share, also beating the $2.85 consensus. Gross booking value (GBV) rose 21% to $27.7 billion, net income hit $1.9 billion, and adjusted EBITDA grew 22% to $2.5 billion, delivering a 52% profit margin.

Operating metrics were equally strong, with a total of 155 million nights booked for stays and experiences in the quarter, up 16% year‑over‑year. Average daily rate (ADR) rose 4% annually, or 5% when currency effects are stripped out. The company said every global region posted double‑digit growth in nights, with North America posting its fastest pace in four years. First‑time bookers grew 13% year‑over‑year, the highest since early 2022, driven especially by Gen‑Z travelers.

All key markets are accelerating. France, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and the United States all saw faster growth versus the prior quarter. Booking nights in Latin America and Asia‑Pacific grew more than 20% year‑over‑year, while EMEA posted mid‑double‑digit growth. Brazil surged over 30%, India more than 60%, and Japan posted growth in the low‑20% range. Bookings made through the mobile app jumped 29% year‑over‑year, now accounting for 66% of total bookings.

Airbnb said the current wave of growth is not driven by a single product but is the result of years of platform‑technology upgrades, operational improvements and product‑experience enhancements. The company launched more than 50 new products and features in the quarter, nearly 70% more than a year ago, with AI accelerating development and testing so new services can be released faster.

AI is also directly improving operational efficiency. Airbnb’s AI customer‑service assistant now supports over 50 languages, and roughly 40% of all support queries in the quarter were resolved without human involvement, up from about one‑third in the prior quarter. Customer‑service cost per reservation fell more than 17% year‑over‑year. The firm is expanding AI‑driven support to voice services in the United States, allowing guests and hosts to get help over the phone.

However, Airbnb’s next step goes beyond using AI for support; it aims to build a dedicated AI agent for travel needs. Chesky told analysts that the company does not view traditional chatbots as suitable for trip planning, nor does it expect consumers to rely on a single AI agent for everything, because travel is inherently about exploration and anticipation. Choosing destinations, browsing accommodations and comparing options are part of the travel experience itself.

Chesky noted that about 80% of travelers enjoy the research phase of a trip. Internal data shows that more than 75% of guests use the platform’s map when selecting a place to stay, over 90% view multiple photos, and 70% read reviews before booking. The average reservation involves roughly three travelers, so accommodation choices often require joint decision‑making.

Airbnb’s own AI agent will use a generative UI rather than a plain text chat. The system can instantly assemble maps, photos, comparison tables, calendars and itineraries from hundreds of travel‑specific UI components, delivering an interface tailored to the guest’s request and letting users explore, compare and book directly within Airbnb.

The company believes its proprietary agent has advantages that generic external AI tools cannot replicate, including nearly two decades of host‑and‑guest market data and the platform’s control over orders, payments and support workflows. This means the AI agent could eventually do more than search for lodging—it could handle reservation changes, payment issues, refunds, re‑bookings and even on‑trip safety assistance. Airbnb plans to roll the agent out to guests in the first half of 2027 and gradually integrate lodging, hotels, services and experiences into a single travel offering.

Beyond AI, Airbnb is expanding its non‑accommodation business. It now offers thousands of boutique and independent hotels in over 60 major destinations worldwide, with hotel bookings growing noticeably faster than its core lodging segment. About 35% of travelers who first book a hotel through Airbnb return to book a stay on the platform within a year. The company is also adding taxi, food‑delivery, laundry, baby‑gear, ski‑equipment and boat‑rental services.

On the partnership front, Airbnb launched an exclusive collaboration with American Express (AXP‑US) in October, feeding more than one million Airbnb listings into Amex Travel. Management said the early phase of the partnership has already generated thousands of bookings, nearly a quarter of which come from first‑time Airbnb users, helping broaden the customer base and attract higher‑end travelers.

Financially, Airbnb generated $1.4 billion of free cash flow in the quarter, bringing the twelve‑month total to $4.9 billion and a free‑cash‑flow margin of 35%. The company repurchased $700 million of its own stock during the quarter; the original buyback authorization still has $2.7 billion remaining, and the board approved an additional up‑to‑$12 billion buyback, reflecting confidence in cash flow and future growth.

The firm also continued to refine its fee structure, completing the final phase of a rate simplification in October that moved almost all hosts onto a single 15.5% service fee. The implied commission rate for the quarter was 17.6%, slightly below the prior year’s level, mainly due to the “Reserve Now, Pay Later” option, which pushes total booking value higher as travelers book earlier, while the related revenue is recognized later.

That payment option also lifted the quarter’s nights‑and‑experiences bookings by roughly three percentage points. Excluding its effect, the underlying year‑over‑year growth would still be about 13%, faster than the second quarter. However, flexible payment and longer lead times also pushed the cancellation rate up from 16% a year ago to 19% this quarter, an increase of roughly 200‑300 basis points, which management will continue to monitor.

Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, Airbnb forecasts revenue between $3.22 billion and $3.28 billion, a 16%‑18% year‑over‑year increase, including roughly two percentage points of favorable currency impact. Gross booking value is expected to grow mid‑double‑digits year‑over‑year, and nights and experience bookings should grow at least low‑double‑digit rates. The company expects adjusted EBITDA to exceed the prior‑year quarter, though profit margins may dip slightly, partly due to timing of marketing expense recognition.

Airbnb also raised its full‑year 2026 outlook, now projecting revenue growth in the high‑teens percent range, up from a prior estimate of at least mid‑teens percent. The target adjusted EBITDA margin was lifted from a floor of 35.5% to roughly 36%.

Chesky said that for a platform of Airbnb’s scale, reigniting rapid growth is rare, and the company is currently in that phase. The earnings show that warming booking demand, more first‑time users and AI‑driven cost reductions have together boosted performance. Going forward, the market will watch whether the proprietary AI agent can further lift conversion rates, expand travel‑service revenue and transform Airbnb from a lodging‑booking site into a one‑stop travel‑service gateway.

items.title: AI熱潮退燒？傳OpenAI募資首筆110億美元到位 估值縮水至1.25兆美元
items.title_en: AI Boom Cools? Report Says OpenAI Secures First $11 Billion of Funding, Valuation Shrinks to $1.25 Trillion
paras: 知情人士周五(6日)透露，OpenAI已完成新一輪募資中的首筆110億美元資金，使公司估值達到1.25兆美元。
路透引述兩名投資人說法報導，目前募得的110億美元僅占OpenAI原先設定募資目標的一部分，原定募資金額最高達300億美元。此外，公司的估值也已從最初尋求的1.5兆美元下修至1.25兆美元。
彭博也引述兩名投資人說法指出，這筆資金周五已匯入OpenAI帳戶，其中剩餘募資金額可能使本輪募資總額增至最高200億美元，預定未來幾周內完成。軟銀(SoftBank)與阿布達比人工智慧投資公司MGX均參與這輪募資。
OpenAI在延後首次公開發行(IPO)計畫後，已與投資人洽談超過一個月，尋求大規模募資，但在AI交易遭遇拋售潮之後，已縮減募資計畫。
募資目標縮減，對這家曾推動當前AI熱潮的募資巨頭而言，代表策略出現明顯轉變。自這輪募資啟動以來，市場投資情緒也已大幅改變，原因包括外界擔憂AI實體基礎設施的支出過於龐大，以及美國期中選舉後，資料中心興建可能面臨新的阻礙。
隨著市場對AI公司的投資情緒持續降溫，部分投資人對OpenAI競爭對手Anthropic預定進行的首次公開發行(IPO)，估值預期約為1.5兆美元，低於先前約2兆美元的預期，醉心更傳出潛在買家目前討論的估值區間約為1.2兆至1.3兆美元。
OpenAI最近一次募資是在今年3月，當時募得1,220億美元，公司估值達8,520億美元。
paras_en: An informed source said on Friday (the 6th) that OpenAI has completed the first $11 billion of its new funding round, bringing the company's valuation to $1.25 trillion.

Reuters, citing two investors, reported that the $11 billion raised so far represents only a portion of OpenAI's original target, which was as high as $30 billion. In addition, the company's valuation has been revised down from the initially sought $1.5 trillion to $1.25 trillion.

Bloomberg also quoted two investors saying the money was transferred to OpenAI's account on Friday, and that the remaining amount could raise the round's total to as much as $20 billion, expected to be completed in the coming weeks. SoftBank and Abu Dhabi AI investment firm MGX both participated in the round.

After postponing its initial public offering (IPO) plan, OpenAI has been in talks with investors for over a month seeking large‑scale funding, but after the AI market experienced a sell‑off, it has scaled back the fundraising plan.

The reduction in the fundraising target signals a clear strategic shift for the fundraising giant that helped spark the current AI boom. Since the round began, market sentiment has also changed dramatically, driven by concerns over the massive spending on AI infrastructure and the possibility that data‑center construction could face new hurdles after the U.S. midterm elections.

As investor enthusiasm for AI companies continues to cool, some investors see the planned IPO of OpenAI rival Anthropic, which is expected to be valued at about $1.5 trillion—down from an earlier estimate of roughly $2 trillion—and rumors suggest potential buyers are currently discussing a valuation range of $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion.
OpenAI's most recent fundraising was in March of this year, when it raised $122 billion and the company was valued at $852 billion.

items.title: 費半跌掉近4成、獲利預估卻大增155% 想撿便宜先過「這一關」
items.title_en: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index Drops Nearly 40%, Yet Profit Forecast Jumps 155% – How to Grab the Discount?
paras: 華爾街有句名言：「投資人切忌盲目猜底，因為便宜之後還可能更便宜。」然而，若估值已降至多年來低點、甚至達到過去幾次市場顯著打底的水平，同時基本面仍保持相對強勁的成長，情況又會如何？
費城半導體指數(SOX) 週四(5日)狂跌 12.2%，創下 2020 年 3 月 16 日以來最慘單日跌幅，30 檔成分股全數收黑。該指數自 2026 年 6 月 22 日創下的 52 週高點 14,655.29 點以來，已大幅修正 38.5%。
然而，半導體業今年的獲利成長，卻與這波猛烈跌勢形成鮮明對比。眼前最直接的問題是，逆勢操作的投資人現在是否該進場布局晶片股？
經歷週四的修正後，費半指數的預估本益比（Forward P/E）已降至 13 倍，為 2019 年 1 月 23 日以來新低，當時該指數收在 1,185.94 點，比週四收盤價低了 87%。
較近的一次低點出現在2022年10月14日，當時費半預估本益比降至13.3倍，指數收在2,162.32點，也在當天結束長達10個月的熊市。
那波熊市期間，費半累計下跌46.5%。預估本益比的計算方式，是將指數價格除以FactSet調查分析師所得的成分股未來12個月加權每股盈餘（EPS）共識預估。
獲利預估大增155% 拉低本益比
回到今年，估值下滑並非因為股價走低。儘管近期遭遇拋售，費半2026年以來仍上漲27.2%。
本益比下降的原因，是作為分母的EPS大幅攀升。在AI基礎建設擴張帶動下，部分權重最高的企業營收與獲利大幅成長，使費半未來12個月滾動加權EPS預估值增加155%。
目前費半預估本益比已不到去年底26.1倍的一半，但華爾街分析師預估，其成分股整體營收在2026至2028年間的年複合成長率將達40.2%，是標普500指數預估營收年複合成長率8.7%的四倍以上。
相較之下，標普500截至周四收盤的預估本益比為17.8倍，明顯高於費半。
估值接近前次谷底 關鍵在獲利能否兌現
Reflexivity共同創辦人Giuseppe Sette透過電子郵件向《MarketWatch》表示，費半目前的估值幾乎與 2022 年 10 月的「歷史絕對底部」相去不遠。
Sette寫道，隨著AI建置支出爆發式成長，「費半在隨後兩年從該水準漲至約3三倍」。他表示：「以那樣的本益比買進，是這十年來布局半導體股的最佳時機之一。」
Sette認為，投資人必須問自己：「你相信這些EPS預估嗎？」
對相信EPS預估能夠實現的長期投資人而言，周四的跌勢或許提供了絕佳買點。Sette總結：「估值已不再是問題，EPS大增155%的成長能否持續，才是關鍵。」
AI晶片仍缺貨 產業展望延伸至2028年
Gabelli 全球科技領航者 ETF(GGTL-US) 基金經理人 Hendi Susanto 則認為：「半導體及半導體設備業的前景在 2026 年剩餘時間乃至 2027 年依然穩健。」
他向 MarketWatch 表示：「2028 年極高機率又會是強勁成長的一年。」
Susanto的預測依據，是超大規模雲端業者高層的說法。這些投入資金擴建AI相關基礎設施的科技巨頭指出，「能源並非首要供應限制」，高階繪圖處理器（GPU）與晶片短缺，才是目前最大的供應挑戰。
Susanto表示，電力與晶片短缺都是「超大規模雲端業者必須克服的瓶頸」，而「相較於晶片，電力建置所需時間更長，前置期也更久」。
記憶體產能售罄 客戶提前鎖定供貨
半導體產業向來具有明顯的景氣循環特性，這也能部分解釋某些業者本益比極低的原因。不過，這一輪科技投資階段的情況，可能有所不同。
Susanto以SK海力士(SKHY-US) 為例，該公司表示，2027年的記憶體產能已全數售罄。他說：「他們正在與主要客戶洽談2028年的供貨協議。客戶提前一年做出承諾，這種情況相當罕見。」
談到周四的市場走勢，Susanto表示，悲觀的投資人著眼於「各種可能性、假設情境」，以及延伸至2028年的風險。
不過，仍有部分投資人看見買進機會，因為他們更關注「供應受限下的強勁需求，以及AI經濟價值的可持續性」。
paras_en: Wall Street has a saying: "Investors should never blindly guess the bottom, because after cheapness it may get even cheaper." However, what if valuations have fallen to multi‑year lows, even reaching levels seen during past major market bottoms, while fundamentals still show relatively strong growth?

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) plunged 12.2% on Thursday the 5th, marking its worst single‑day drop since March 16, 2020, with all 30 component stocks closing in the red. Since its 52‑week high of 14,655.29 on June 22, 2026, the index has corrected 38.5%.

Yet the semiconductor sector’s profit growth this year stands in stark contrast to the sharp decline. The immediate question is whether contrarian investors should now enter and position themselves in chip stocks?
After Thursday’s correction, the index’s forward P/E fell to 13‑times, the lowest since January 23, 2019, when the index closed at 1,185.94 points – 87% below Thursday’s close.
A more recent low occurred on October 14, 2022, when the forward P/E slipped to 13.3‑times and the index closed at 2,162.32 points, ending a ten‑month bear market that day.

During that bear market the index fell a cumulative 46.5%. The forward P/E is calculated by dividing the index price by the consensus 12‑month weighted EPS forecast for its components, as surveyed by FactSet analysts.
Profit forecasts have surged 155%, pulling the P/E down
Returning to this year, the valuation decline is not due to a price drop. Despite recent sell‑offs, the index has risen 27.2% since the start of 2026.

The P/E fell because the EPS denominator rose sharply. Driven by AI infrastructure expansion, revenue and earnings of several top‑weight companies have surged, lifting the 12‑month rolling weighted EPS estimate for the index by 155%.

The current forward P/E is now less than half of the 26.1‑times level at the end of last year, yet Wall Street analysts project a 40.2% compound annual revenue growth for the components from 2026 to 2028 – more than four times the S&P 500’s projected 8.7% CAGR.
By comparison, the S&P 500’s forward P/E at Thursday’s close was 17.8‑times, clearly higher than the semiconductor index.
Valuation is near the previous trough – the key is whether earnings can be delivered
Giuseppe Sette, co‑founder of Reflexivity, told MarketWatch by email that the SOX’s current valuation is not far from the “historical absolute bottom” seen in October 2022.

Sette wrote that with AI spending exploding, “the index could climb from that level to roughly three‑times that within the next two years.” He added: “Buying at that P/E is one of the best times in the past decade to position for semiconductor stocks.”
Sette believes investors must ask themselves: “Do you believe these EPS forecasts?”

For long‑term investors who trust the EPS outlook, Thursday’s drop may present an excellent entry point. Sette summed up: “Valuation is no longer the issue; the real question is whether the 155% EPS growth can be sustained.”
AI chips remain in short supply – industry outlook extends to 2028

Gabelli Global Technology Leaders ETF (GGTL‑US) fund manager Hendi Susanto says: “The outlook for semiconductors and semiconductor equipment remains solid through the remainder of 2026 and into 2027.”
He told MarketWatch: “2028 is also very likely to be a strong growth year.”

Susanto’s view is based on statements from senior executives at hyperscale cloud providers. These tech giants, investing heavily in AI‑related infrastructure, say “energy is not the primary supply constraint,” and that shortages of high‑end GPUs and chips are the biggest current challenges.

Susanto notes that both power and chip shortages are “bottlenecks that hyperscale cloud providers must overcome,” and that “building power capacity takes longer and has a longer lead time than chip production.”
Memory capacity sold out – customers lock in supply early
The semiconductor industry is known for pronounced cyclical patterns, which partly explains why some companies have extremely low P/Es. However, this round of tech investment may be different.

Using SK Hynix (SKHY‑US) as an example, Susanto says the company has already sold out its memory capacity for 2027. He adds: “They are negotiating supply agreements for 2028 with major customers, who are committing a year in advance – a rare situation.”
Commenting on Thursday’s market move, Susanto said pessimistic investors focus on “various possibilities, hypothetical scenarios,” and risks that extend to 2028.
Nevertheless, some investors see buying opportunities because they are more focused on “strong demand despite supply constraints and the sustainability of AI’s economic value.”

items.title: 油輪運費暴漲美墨灣煉廠享重油折價、S-Oil長約減壓
items.title_en: Tanker Freight Surge Gives Gulf Coast Refineries Heavy‑Oil Discount, S‑Oil Mitigates Impact with Long‑Term Charters
paras: 2026年11月07日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 國際油輪運費大漲，讓靠近產油地的美國墨西哥灣煉油廠取得較便宜的原料，也拉開與亞洲同業的成本差距。不過，亞洲業者受到的影響並不相同：南韓S-Oil透過長期租船減輕衝擊，台塑化(6505-TW)則表示，高運費已限制原油採購選擇，並吃掉部分煉油利潤。
瓦萊羅能源Valero Energy(VLO-US)指出，超大型油輪將原油從美國墨西哥灣運往亞洲的費用，已從2025年平均每桶約5美元，升至30至35美元。運送成本大增後，原油賣方必須降低售價，才能減輕遠方買家的負擔。
美墨灣煉油廠靠近產地，不必負擔同樣高昂的跨洋運費，卻能買到價格較低的原油。菲利普斯66 Phillips 66(PSX-US)表示，公司中部與美墨灣沿岸煉油廠可透過管線取得加拿大原油，多數廠區也具備加工重油的能力。
加拿大西部精選原油(WCS)通常比美國西德州原油(WTI)便宜。當兩者價格差距擴大，使用加拿大重油的煉油廠，原料成本相對於市場基準就更有利。
亞洲煉油廠則必須更留意運輸安排。S-Oil是南韓主要煉油業者，位於蔚山溫山的煉油廠每天可處理66.9萬桶原油。公司表示，多數原油透過長約向沙烏地阿拉伯採購，約65%的運輸合約採長期租船，因此第三季平均運費與前季相近，即期運價上漲的影響有限。
S-Oil第三季煉油部門營業利益達6,904億韓元，季增29.7%。公司指出，外銷油品價差強勁、油價上漲帶來成本遞延效益，以及歲修後稼動率回升，支撐當季獲利。
台塑化則表示，運費過高使非洲與美國原油難以運往亞洲。總經理林克彥先前指出，以中東原油計算，扣除運費與保險後的淨煉油利潤仍高於每桶10美元，但運輸成本已吃掉部分利潤。
台塑化第三季煉油營運仍較前季改善。公司表示，中東原油到貨回穩，使煉油產能利用率由第二季的66.5%升至91.2%；原油耗用成本下降，加上全球成品油供應吃緊、外銷油品價差擴大，支撐煉油事業營業利益成長。

paras_en: November 7, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center) – International tanker freight has jumped dramatically, allowing U.S. Gulf‑of‑Mexico refineries near the production area to obtain cheaper crude and widening the cost gap with Asian peers. However, Asian players are affected differently: South Korea’s S‑Oil eases the shock through long‑term charter contracts, while Formosa Plastics Corp. (6505‑TW) says high freight limits crude‑sourcing options and erodes part of refining margins.

Valero Energy (VLO‑US) reported that the cost to ship crude from the U.S. Gulf of Mexico to Asia on ultra‑large tankers has risen from about $5 per barrel on average in 2025 to $30‑35 per barrel. With transport costs soaring, crude sellers must cut prices to ease the burden on distant buyers.

Gulf‑of‑Mexico refineries, being close to the source, avoid the same steep trans‑ocean freight and can buy lower‑priced crude. Phillips 66 (PSX‑US) said its mid‑continent and Gulf‑coast plants can obtain Canadian crude via pipelines, and most of its sites have the capability to process heavy oil.

Western Canadian Select (WCS) crude is usually cheaper than U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI). When the price gap widens, refineries using Canadian heavy oil enjoy a material cost advantage relative to market benchmarks.

Asian refiners must pay closer attention to logistics. S‑Oil, South Korea’s leading refiner, operates a Ulsan‑Wonsan complex that can process 669,000 barrels per day. The company said most of its crude is procured from Saudi Arabia under long‑term contracts, with about 65% of its shipping secured by long‑term charters, so third‑quarter average freight rates remained similar to the prior quarter, limiting the impact of spot‑rate spikes.

S‑Oil’s third‑quarter refining segment operating profit reached 690.4 billion won, up 29.7% sequentially. The company attributed the gain to strong export‑product spreads, cost‑deferral benefits from higher oil prices, and a rebound in operating rates after scheduled maintenance.

Formosa Plastics Corp. said excessive freight makes it difficult to ship African and U.S. crude to Asia. General manager Lin K‑Yen previously noted that, using Middle‑East crude as a reference, net refining profit after deducting freight and insurance still exceeds $10 per barrel, but transportation costs have already eaten into that margin.

Formosa Plastics’ third‑quarter refining operations improved versus the prior quarter. The firm said stable deliveries of Middle‑East crude lifted refinery capacity utilization from 66.5% in Q2 to 91.2%; lower crude‑consumption costs, together with tight global product‑fuel supplies and wider export spreads, supported growth in refining operating profit.

items.title: 錫價一度跌至8個月低點低庫存仍推升近月溢價
items.title_en: Tin price hits 8‑month low, low inventories still drive near‑month premium
paras: 2026年11月07日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 科技股賣壓波及金屬市場，倫敦金屬交易所(LME)三個月期錫一週內從每公噸5萬美元以上，一度跌至45,360美元，創8個月低點。不過，錫價下跌並未伴隨庫存回升，近月交貨價格反而高於遠月，顯示市場對AI需求的預期降溫，與眼前供應偏緊同時存在。
6日盤中，倫敦錫期貨上漲1.7%至每公噸46,250美元，前一日則下跌3.2%。另一方面，LME現金錫相對三個月期錫的價差，從8月每公噸貼水逾350美元，轉為升水125美元，為去年12月以來最高，反映即期交貨需求相對吃緊。
庫存持續下降是近月溢價擴大的背景。LME註冊錫庫存降至3,885公噸，為去年12月以來最低；上海期貨交易所庫存則從6月的12,358公噸降至4,004公噸。即使期貨價格走低，兩地交易所的可見庫存仍處低檔。
全球最大精煉錫出口國印尼今年加強打擊非法採礦，前三季精煉錫出口量年減14%，降至32,800公噸。不過，印尼錫業公司PT Timah(TINS)10月30日公布，前三季精煉錫產量年增49%至16,190公噸，銷量年增72%至16,304公噸，出口占銷量96%。公司表示，產量成長來自陸地與海上採礦作業改善，包括增加採礦單位、開闢工作區及提升船舶與設備效率，並在政府專責小組支持下加強礦區管理。
需求端則尚未出現足以對應AI投資熱度的用錫增幅。國際錫業協會(ITA)資深市場分析師Tom Langston表示，AI資料中心仍是長期需求動能，但尚未帶來實際消費量的躍升，今年較大的影響仍在投資人情緒。中國太陽能新增裝置成長放緩，也使相關用錫需求降溫。

paras_en: On November 7, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – Selling pressure in tech stocks spilled over into the metals market, and LME three‑month tin futures fell from above $50,000 per metric ton to as low as $45,360 within a week, marking an eight‑month low. However, the price drop was not accompanied by a rebound in inventories; near‑month delivery prices were actually higher than far‑month prices, indicating that expectations for AI‑driven demand are cooling while supply remains tight.

During intraday trading on the 6th, London tin futures rose 1.7% to $46,250 per metric ton after a 3.2% decline the previous day. Meanwhile, the basis between LME cash tin and three‑month futures swung from a discount of more than $350 per ton in August to a premium of $125, the highest since December last year, reflecting tighter demand for spot deliveries.

Continuing inventory declines underpin the widening near‑month premium. LME‑registered tin stocks fell to 3,885 metric tons, the lowest level since December last year; Shanghai Futures Exchange inventories dropped from 12,358 metric tons in June to 4,004 metric tons. Even as futures prices fell, visible inventories on both exchanges remain at historically low levels.

Indonesia, the world’s largest refined tin exporter, stepped up crackdowns on illegal mining this year, with refined tin exports down 14% year‑on‑year to 32,800 metric tons for the first three quarters. However, PT Timah (TINS) announced on October 30 that refined tin production rose 49% year‑on‑year to 16,190 metric tons and sales increased 72% to 16,304 metric tons, with exports accounting for 96% of sales. The company said the production boost stemmed from improvements in both land and offshore mining operations, including more mining units, expanded work areas, and higher ship and equipment efficiency, supported by a government‑led task force overseeing mine management.

On the demand side, the increase in tin usage has not yet matched the hype around AI investment. Tom Langston, senior market analyst at the International Tin Association (ITA), said AI data centers remain a long‑term demand driver but have not yet translated into a noticeable jump in actual consumption; this year’s larger impact is still on investor sentiment. Slower growth in new solar installations in China also dampens related tin demand.

items.title: 晶片股遭遇2020年來最慘一日！30大龍頭28檔陷熊市 CoreWeave信用風險竄高
items.title_en: Chip Stocks Face Their Worst Day Since 2020! 28 of 30 Leaders in Bear Market, CoreWeave Credit Risk Soars
paras: 晶片股遭遇2020年以來最慘烈的一個交易日，產業信用市場也同步亮起警訊。30檔主要晶片股中，已有28檔陷入熊市，反映市場對人工智慧(AI)投資熱潮及相關企業融資風險的疑慮升高。不過，從信用市場的變化來看，壓力並非中期選舉結果突然引發，而是早已逐步累積。
投資級企業的信用利差擴大已持續數月。自4月中旬以來，亞馬遜 (Amazon.com) (AMZN-US) 五年期信用違約互換(CDS)價格接近翻倍，升至100個基點；Alphabet (GOOGL-US) 的CDS價格也從47個基點升至92個基點，顯示市場要求大型科技企業提供更高的信用風險補償。
然而，真正承受較大壓力的並非這些大型雲端業者，而是信用評級較低、融資結構更複雜的新雲端服務商。信用市場人士Nolan指出，CoreWeave (CRWV-US) 是北美交易流動性較高的單一名稱高收益CDS之一，其合約即期支付點數周四升至23點，高於前一日的20點，4月中旬時則僅有2點。這類即期點數報價通常用於信用狀況較差的企業，反映投資人對其債務風險的憂慮明顯升高。
Nolan表示，CoreWeave在美國期中選舉前就已面臨壓力，因此不能將近期信用風險升高歸因於選舉結果。問題核心之一在於公司的資本結構：其CDS所參考的是高級無擔保債務，但CoreWeave同時透過槓桿貸款、資產支持交易及私募信貸取得資金，而這些債務的清償順位都優先於公司債。
換言之，一旦企業陷入財務困境，高級無擔保債券持有人可能排在其他債權人之後，面臨更高的本金損失風險。因此，投資人要求更高的風險補償，也使CoreWeave的信用違約互換價格大幅攀升。Nolan直言，目前新雲端服務商(neocloud)已成為市場信用壓力最集中的領域。
相較之下，超大型雲端服務商(hyperscalers)大部分資本支出由營運現金流支應，信用體質仍相對穩健。CoreWeave則是高度聚焦AI業務的企業，客戶來源較為集中，對產業投資趨勢及融資環境變化也更為敏感。這種商業模式與資金結構的差異，使市場對大型科技公司與新雲端業者的信用風險評價逐漸分化。
值得注意的是，資本支出放緩未必對債權人不利。Nolan指出，超大型雲端服務商近期大量發債，債券供給已讓投資人難以消化，部分解釋了信用利差持續擴大的原因。若未來資料中心及AI基礎建設投資速度放慢，從信用風險角度來看，反而未必是壞事，因為企業可能因此減少新增融資需求，降低債務負擔持續攀升的壓力。
不過，Nolan並未預測資本支出是否真的會放緩，也強調目前仍有待觀察。整體而言，晶片股大跌只是市場重新評估AI產業風險的一個面向，信用市場更值得關注的訊號，是大型科技企業與新雲端服務商之間的融資能力、資本結構及償債風險正出現明顯落差。
paras_en: Chip stocks endured their most severe trading day since 2020, and the industry credit market lit up warning signals at the same time. Among 30 major chip stocks, 28 have already slipped into a bear market, reflecting growing doubts about the AI investment frenzy and financing risks of related firms. However, the pressure in the credit market did not arise suddenly from the mid‑term election results; it has been building up gradually.

Investment‑grade companies have seen their credit spreads widen for several months. Since mid‑April, Amazon (AMZN‑US) five‑year credit default swap (CDS) prices have nearly doubled, climbing to 100 basis points, while Alphabet’s (GOOGL‑US) CDS price rose from 47 to 92 basis points, indicating the market demands higher credit‑risk compensation from large tech firms.

The real strain, however, is not on these big cloud providers but on lower‑rated, more complexly financed new cloud service firms. Credit‑market analyst Nolan notes that CoreWeave (CRWV‑US) is one of the more liquid high‑yield CDS names in North America, with its spot CDS points jumping to 23 on Thursday, up from 20 the day before and just 2 points in mid‑April. Such spot quotes are typically used for companies with weaker credit, reflecting a clear rise in investor concern over its debt risk.

Nolan says CoreWeave was already under pressure before the U.S. midterm elections, so the recent rise in credit risk cannot be blamed on the election outcome. A core issue lies in the company’s capital structure: its CDS references senior unsecured debt, yet CoreWeave also raises funds through leveraged loans, asset‑backed transactions and private credit, all of which rank ahead of corporate bonds in repayment priority.

In other words, if the firm hits financial distress, senior unsecured bondholders could be pushed behind other creditors, facing higher principal loss risk. Investors therefore demand higher risk compensation, driving CoreWeave’s CDS price sharply higher. Nolan bluntly states that new cloud providers (neocloud) have become the sector with the most concentrated credit pressure.

By contrast, hyperscale cloud providers fund most of their capex from operating cash flow, keeping their credit profiles relatively sound. CoreWeave is a highly AI‑focused company with a concentrated customer base, making it more sensitive to industry investment trends and financing‑environment shifts. These business‑model and funding‑structure differences are causing credit‑risk assessments for big tech firms and new cloud players to diverge.

It is worth noting that slower capex does not necessarily hurt creditors. Nolan points out that hyperscalers have recently issued large amounts of debt, flooding the bond market and making it hard for investors to absorb, which partly explains the ongoing spread widening. If data‑center and AI‑infrastructure investment slows, from a credit‑risk perspective it may not be a bad thing, as firms could reduce new financing needs and ease the pressure of rising debt burdens.

However, Nolan does not forecast whether capex will truly slow and stresses that the situation remains to be seen. Overall, the chip‑stock plunge is just one facet of the market’s reassessment of AI‑industry risk; a more telling signal from the credit market is the growing gap in financing capacity, capital structure and debt‑service risk between large tech giants and new cloud service providers.

items.title: 1998還是2000？高盛：AI股暴跌更像LTCM危機而非網路泡沫化 但最大疑問仍是投資回報
items.title_en: 1998 or 2000? Goldman Sachs: AI Stock Crash Looks More Like the LTCM Crisis Than the Dot‑Com Bubble, but the Biggest Question Remains Investment Returns
paras: 美股科技股近期遭遇劇烈拋售，市場開始爭論，這波跌勢究竟更接近1998年長期資本管理公司(LTCM)危機引發的流動性衝擊，還是2000年網路泡沫破裂的前兆？高盛Delta One交易主管Rich Privorotsky傾向前者，但他也指出，AI投資熱潮能否產生足以匹配龐大資本支出的營收，仍是市場尚未解答的關鍵問題。
美股周四(5日)遭遇重挫，納斯達克指數單日下跌5.5%，費城半導體指數重挫12%，標普500指數下跌4.4%，創2025年4月以來最大單日跌幅。高盛波動性恐慌指數升至滿分10分中的9.3分，衡量波動率波動程度的VVIX單日飆升近45點，寫下歷史第二大單日漲幅，僅次於2018年的「波動末日」事件。
這波賣壓的直接導火線，是民主黨在期中選舉取得勝利後，市場重新評估美國資料中心建設前景，尤其德州等州可能加強監管，令投資人擔憂AI基礎設施擴張速度放緩。不過，Privorotsky認為，周四跌勢不只是基本面重新定價，也受到槓桿ETF、程式交易及做市商避險部位共同推動。
Privorotsky指出，半導體及納斯達克100指數相關槓桿ETF在收盤前觸發機械式賣單，加上做市商持有負Gamma部位，形成價格下跌、避險賣壓增加，再進一步壓低市場的自我強化效應。
野村證券策略師Charlie McElligott估算，周四槓桿ETF賣出規模達470億美元，波動率控制基金賣出約610億美元；做市商每當標普500下跌1%，便面臨約70億美元的負Gamma曝險。
高盛美國銷售交易員Ariana Contessa在當日資金流向與持倉報告中指出，VIX單日大漲67%，升至27.77，高盛多個AI相關投資組合當天創下ChatGPT推出以來最大單日跌幅。
程式交易賣壓也可能延續。標普500期貨收盤跌破CTA中期交易門檻7549點，高盛以指數下跌2.5個標準差的情境估算，未來一周標普500可能面臨逾74.8億美元程式化賣壓；瑞銀則警告，風險控制基金周四單日賣出規模可能超過1000億美元。
然而，Privorotsky認為，真正值得擔憂的並非只有程式賣盤，而是市場買盤明顯不足。高盛現股交易部門周四淨賣出30億美元，其中科技股占22億美元，使科技股累計淨賣出規模達270億美元，已超過2025年7月市場技術性修正期間的210億美元。
Contessa表示，客戶詢問市場的熱度達到滿分10分，但實際交易活躍程度只有5分，ETF交易量占當日市場總成交量32%。尤其周三曾支撐大盤的大型科技股，周四幾乎沒有出現相應的買盤承接。
Privorotsky指出，真正的問題是底層需求不足，尤其缺乏長期基金進場承接。他觀察到，多策略基金、量化基金、長線基金及散戶似乎都朝同一方向減碼，當市場缺少願意逆勢買進的資金時，賣壓便更容易放大。
對於這波跌勢是否代表AI泡沫破裂，Privorotsky更傾向將其比作1998年LTCM危機。當年俄羅斯違約及LTCM崩盤引發金融市場流動性緊縮，但美國經濟成長基本面仍然穩健，之後隨著流動性恢復及聯準會降息，市場迅速收復失土。
他認為，目前AI產業的成長引擎可能仍然完好，市場只是在重新評估資料中心建設的融資能力、支出速度與時間表。支持這項看法的重要理由，是當前大型科技企業與2000年網路泡沫時期的公司不同，已經具備實際營收、現金流及相對穩健的資產負債表。
高盛TMT交易員Peter Callahan指出，半導體指數估值倍數相較6月至7月高點已壓縮約50%。輝達 (NVIDIA) (NVDA-US)未來24個月預估本益比約10倍，為2013年以來最低；相較之下，2000年網路泡沫高峰時，思科 (Cisco) (CSCO-US)本益比曾超過100倍。
不過，Privorotsky也承認，當前市場與2000年網路泡沫仍有令人不安的相似之處，尤其是資本支出規模龐大，投資回報卻高度不確定。他提出的核心問題是，市場究竟只是在拋售一個基本面健康的成長故事，還是開始發現這套AI投資模式在經濟上根本難以成立？他目前傾向前者，但認為需求、產能利用率及投資回報都必須接受檢驗。
Privorotsky將AI投資風險歸納為四大問題，包括融資能力是否足以支撐建設規模、營收能否證明資本投入合理、電力與許可是否足以支撐算力擴張，以及整體資本支出軌跡是否能夠持續。
他認為，市場目前過度聚焦第三項，也就是電力供應與建設許可限制，這反而可能是四項風險中相對次要的問題。供給受到限制，不代表市場需求消失，真正需要檢驗的是企業未來營收能否匹配投入的資本。
相較之下，融資問題已經浮現警訊。根據高盛投資人關係團隊統計，超大型科技公司今年已發行約2960億美元債券，高於高盛原先預估的全年2500億美元，也占全球投資級債券供給約9%。
與此同時，資料中心相關信用違約交換(CDS)周四突破500個基點，創下歷史新高；AI雲端運算業者CoreWeave (CRWV-US)的債券利差也超過1200個基點，顯示市場對相關企業融資風險的疑慮升高。
Privorotsky警告，電力供應與建設許可延誤，可能進一步推高資料中心融資成本。每延後一季取得許可，尚未完工的資料中心就可能多承擔一季利息支出，形成建設延宕與融資成本上升的惡性循環。
政治與監管變化也是市場重新定價的關鍵。高盛估算，各州可能採取的資料中心暫停建設措施，涉及約45%的美國計畫資料中心產能，其中德州約占四分之一。市場擔心，若各州限制建設，將延後AI基礎設施擴張，進而影響晶片、伺服器及雲端服務需求。
不過，Privorotsky認為，市場可能過度解讀德州候任州長Gina Hinojosa的監管立場。她曾表示，推動經濟發展與保障德州居民利益並不衝突，也強調自己並非反對資料中心。Privorotsky認為，這更像是監管規則重新調整，而非政治上全面排斥資料中心，實際支出可能高於市場目前折價反映的程度。
高盛投資人關係團隊另引述《CNBC》報導指出，Hinojosa已表示，取得許可的資料中心將獲准完工，這可能保障2027年及2028年大部分建設進度。高盛經濟學家也預期，相關暫停措施可能不會持續太久，因為資料中心議題在選民關注事項中的優先順序相對較低。
但地方反彈情緒確實升高。Jefferies援引Heatmap調查指出，強烈反對在自家住所附近興建資料中心的美國民眾比例，已從2025年9月的24%升至2026年8月的61%。除了德州，喬治亞州、俄亥俄州及密西根州也正關注類似立法動向。德州立法會期將持續至2027年5月31日，相關監管調整仍可能影響後續建設規劃。
Privorotsky最後也提醒，1998年的歷史類比有一項重要限制：當年市場反彈的重要推力，是聯準會恢復流動性並連續降息。1998年時任聯準會主席葛林斯潘在七周內三度降息，但目前市場環境並不相同，不能直接假設聯準會會再次提供同樣的支撐。
報導指出，當時市場對聯準會12月升息的機率定價約為65%，克里夫蘭聯邦準備銀行總裁Hammack周四上午也公開表達維持限制性貨幣政策的傾向。這意味著，即使市場出現流動性壓力，也未必能像1998年一樣迅速獲得降息支援。
Privorotsky另援引歷史統計指出，自1950年以來，標普500在19次美國期中選舉後的12個月內都錄得上漲，但這項統計並不代表市場短期內一定會反彈。他認為，歷史經驗顯示選舉後的市場波動可能提供布局機會，但投資人仍難以精準掌握進場時點。
整體而言，這波AI股拋售可能同時包含程式交易引發的流動性衝擊，以及市場對資料中心融資、建設進度與投資回報的基本面疑慮。1998年的LTCM危機或許是較接近的歷史參照，但在長線資金尚未重新進場、AI營收能否支撐巨額資本支出仍不明朗之際，市場也不能排除經歷更長時間估值調整的可能。
paras_en: U.S. tech stocks have recently faced a sharp sell‑off, sparking a market debate over whether this decline resembles the liquidity shock triggered by the 1998 Long‑Term Capital Management (LTCM) crisis or the early warning signs of the 2000 dot‑com bust. Goldman Sachs Delta One trading head Rich Privorotsky leans toward the former, but he also notes that the key unanswered question is whether the AI investment frenzy can generate enough revenue to match its massive capital outlays.

On Thursday (the 5th), U.S. equities slumped hard: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% in a single day, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12%, and the S&P 500 dropped 4.4%, marking the biggest one‑day decline since April 2025. Goldman’s volatility‑fear index jumped to 9.3 out of 10, and the VVIX, which measures volatility‑of‑volatility, surged nearly 45 points in one day – the second‑largest one‑day jump on record, behind only the 2018 “volatility apocalypse.”

The immediate trigger for the sell‑off was the market’s reassessment of U.S. data‑center construction prospects after the Democrats won the mid‑term elections, especially concerns that states such as Texas might tighten regulation, slowing the pace of AI‑infrastructure expansion. Privorotsky, however, believes Thursday’s decline was not just a fundamental repricing but was also driven by leveraged ETFs, algorithmic trading, and market‑maker hedging positions.

Privorotsky explained that leveraged ETFs tied to semiconductors and the Nasdaq‑100 triggered mechanical sell orders before the close, and market makers holding negative‑gamma positions added further price‑drop pressure, creating a self‑reinforcing downward spiral.

Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott estimated that leveraged ETFs sold about $47 billion on Thursday, volatility‑control funds shed roughly $61 billion, and market makers faced about $7 billion of negative‑gamma exposure for each 1% drop in the S&P 500.

Goldman U.S. sales trader Ariana Contessa noted in the day‑of‑flow and positioning report that the VIX surged 67% in a single session to 27.77, and several Goldman AI‑focused portfolios recorded their largest single‑day declines since ChatGPT’s launch.

Algorithmic selling pressure could persist. The S&P 500 futures closed below the CTA mid‑term trading threshold of 7,549 points. Using a scenario where the index falls 2.5 standard deviations, Goldman estimates that programmed sell pressure could exceed $7.48 billion over the next week; UBS warned that risk‑control funds may have sold more than $100 billion on Thursday alone.

Privorotsky, however, stresses that the real worry is not just algorithmic selling but a stark lack of buying. Goldman’s cash‑equity desk net‑sold $3 billion on Thursday, $2.2 billion of which was in tech stocks, bringing cumulative net tech‑stock sales to $27 billion—already surpassing the $21 billion sold during the technical correction in July 2025.

Contessa said clients rated market heat at a full 10 out of 10, yet actual trading activity was only a 5. The day’s ETF volume accounted for 32% of total market turnover. Large‑cap tech stocks that had supported the market on Wednesday saw almost no buying support on Thursday.

Privorotsky pointed out that the core issue is insufficient underlying demand, especially a shortage of long‑term fund inflows. He observed that multi‑strategy funds, quant funds, long‑term funds and retail investors all appear to be cutting exposure in the same direction; when there is no capital willing to buy against the tide, sell pressure amplifies.

Regarding whether the slump signals an AI bubble burst, Privorotsky likens it more to the 1998 LTCM crisis. Back then, Russia’s default and LTCM’s collapse triggered a liquidity crunch in financial markets, yet the U.S. economy’s fundamentals remained solid, and the market recovered quickly as liquidity returned and the Fed cut rates.

He believes the AI industry’s growth engine may still be intact; the market is merely re‑evaluating data‑center financing capacity, spending speed and timelines. A key reason for this view is that today’s large tech firms differ from those of the 2000 dot‑com era, now boasting real revenue, cash flow and relatively strong balance sheets.

Goldman TMT trader Peter Callahan noted that semiconductor index valuation multiples have compressed about 50% from their June‑July peaks. Nvidia (NVDA‑US) is projected to trade at a forward P/E of roughly 10× over the next 24 months—the lowest since 2013—whereas Cisco (CSCO‑US) topped 100× during the height of the dot‑com bubble.

Privorotsky also acknowledges unsettling parallels with the 2000 bubble, particularly the massive scale of capital spending coupled with highly uncertain returns. He frames the central question as whether the market is merely dumping a fundamentally healthy growth story or beginning to see that the AI investment model is economically untenable. He currently leans toward the former but says demand, capacity utilization and returns must all be tested.

He categorizes AI investment risk into four main issues: whether financing can sustain construction scale, whether revenue can justify the capital outlay, whether power and permits are sufficient for compute expansion, and whether the overall cap‑ex trajectory is sustainable.

Privorotsky argues the market is over‑focused on the third issue—power supply and construction permits—which may actually be the least critical of the four risks. Supply constraints do not imply demand disappearance; the real test is whether future revenues can match the invested capital.

By contrast, financing concerns are already sounding alarms. Goldman’s investor‑relations team tallied that ultra‑large tech companies have issued about $296 billion in bonds this year, exceeding the firm’s original $250 billion full‑year estimate and representing roughly 9% of global investment‑grade bond supply.

At the same time, data‑center‑related credit default swaps spiked past 500 basis points on Thursday, a historic high; AI cloud‑computing provider CoreWeave (CRWV‑US) saw its bond spread widen beyond 1,200 basis points, reflecting heightened market worries about financing risk for related firms.

Privorotsky warned that delays in power supply and construction permits could further raise data‑center financing costs. Each quarter a permit is postponed adds another quarter of interest expense to unfinished data centers, creating a vicious cycle of construction delays and higher financing costs.

Political and regulatory shifts are also key to the market’s re‑pricing. Goldman estimates that state‑level data‑center pause measures could affect about 45% of planned U.S. data‑center capacity, with Texas alone accounting for roughly a quarter of that exposure.

However, Privorotsky thinks the market may be over‑interpreting the stance of Texas gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa. She has said that promoting economic development does not conflict with protecting Texas residents and stressed she is not opposed to data centers. Privorotsky sees this more as a regulatory adjustment than a blanket political rejection, suggesting actual spending could be higher than the market’s current discount reflects.

Goldman’s investor‑relations team also cited a CNBC report that Hinojosa has indicated data centers that obtain permits will be allowed to complete construction, which could safeguard most of the 2027‑2028 build‑out schedule. Goldman economists expect any pause measures to be short‑lived, as data‑center issues rank relatively low on voters’ priority lists.

Nonetheless, local opposition is rising. Jefferies, citing a Heatmap survey, reported that the share of Americans strongly opposed to having a data center near their home jumped from 24% in September 2025 to 61% in August 2026. Beyond Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Michigan are also watching similar legislative moves. The Texas legislative session runs through May 31 2027, and related regulatory tweaks could still affect future construction plans.

Privorotsky cautions that the 1998 historical analogy has a key limitation: the rebound then was driven by the Fed restoring liquidity and cutting rates three times over seven weeks under Chairman Alan Greenspan. The current environment is different, so one cannot assume the Fed will provide the same support again.

The report notes that at the time the market priced a roughly 65% probability of a Fed rate hike in December, and Cleveland Fed President Loretta Hammack publicly signaled a preference for maintaining a restrictive monetary stance on Thursday morning. This suggests that even if liquidity pressure returns, rate cuts may not come as swiftly as they did in 1998.

Privorotsky also referenced historical data showing that since 1950, the S&P 500 has risen in the 12 months following each of the 19 U.S. mid‑term elections, but this statistic does not guarantee a short‑term rebound. He believes history shows post‑election market volatility can offer positioning opportunities, yet investors still struggle to time entries precisely.

Overall, the AI‑stock sell‑off likely combines algorithmic‑driven liquidity shocks with fundamental concerns over data‑center financing, construction timelines and investment returns. The 1998 LTCM crisis may be the closer historical reference, but with long‑term capital not yet back in the market and AI revenue still uncertain, the market cannot rule out a prolonged valuation adjustment.

items.title: 民主黨橫掃國會後 微軟出售Xbox可能性擴大
items.title_en: After the Democrats Sweep Congress, the Likelihood of Microsoft Selling Xbox Increases
paras: 美國民主黨在期中選舉奪下參眾兩院控制權後，遊戲產業分析師 Joost van Dreunen 認為，資料中心建設面臨的政治阻力，可能促使微軟 (MSFT-US) 重新檢視資源配置，增加出售 Xbox 業務的可能性。不過，這項判斷仍屬策略推測，微軟此前已明確回應，Xbox 並未求售。
《Wccftech》週五 (6 日) 報導，市場研究公司 SuperData Research 共同創辦人、紐約大學史登商學院教授 van Dreunen，在 Substack 文章中提出，選民對資料中心擴張的不滿，加上 Xbox 營收承壓，可能成為微軟重新評估遊戲事業策略地位的背景。
但目前尚無微軟啟動出售程序的公開證據。這項分析的關鍵，在於政策變化是否會改變微軟對旗下業務的取捨，而非選舉結果直接導致 Xbox 出售。
資料中心政策風險升溫 分析師關注資源配置
van Dreunen 引述《華爾街日報》報導指出，美國超過 40 個城鎮及郡在此次選舉中，將資料中心相關措施交付選民表決，其中至少 10 個地方通過限制措施或全面禁令。
他另引述一項涵蓋逾 7.9 萬名登記選民的全國調查，指出 56% 受訪者將候選人對人工智慧 (AI) 與資料中心的立場，視為影響投票選擇的重要因素。部分新當選的民主黨籍州長，也已承諾暫停核發新許可，或終止新建資料中心的租稅優惠。
這些措施若付諸實施，可能影響科技公司的建設時程與投資成本。不過，地方公投、州政府政策與聯邦國會權力分屬不同層級，民主黨掌握國會，並不代表美國將立即實施全國性的資料中心限制。
van Dreunen 認為，微軟已將 AI 基礎建設列為重要投資方向，若擴張環境變得更複雜，管理階層可能重新衡量各項業務的策略價值，Xbox 因而可能受到檢視。
然而，資料中心建設受阻，也可能使微軟延後支出，未必會增加出售資產的需求。因此，政策風險與出售 Xbox 之間，仍缺乏直接的因果證據。
Xbox營收承壓 成為出售推測背景
除了政策變化，遊戲業務的成長表現，也是 van Dreunen 提出這項判斷的重要因素。
報導指出，Xbox 營收持續下滑，雖然降幅已有收斂，但表現仍落後部分其他業務；相較之下，微軟搜尋與廣告業務 2026 年營收成長 10%。
微軟近年也曾在遊戲部門裁員、關閉工作室。不過，這些調整本身不足以證明公司準備出售 Xbox，也不能直接認定相關措施是為了將資金轉投入 AI。
營收下滑同樣只是評估業務價值的其中一項指標。微軟是否繼續持有 Xbox，仍涉及獲利能力、現金流、旗下遊戲智慧財產權 (IP)，以及與訂閱、雲端服務的整合效益。
傳私募買家探詢 微軟否認求售
《The Information》數週前曾報導，已有未具名私募股權買家探詢收購 Xbox 的可能性，對該業務的估值約為 1,000 億至 1,500 億美元。
這項消息顯示，Xbox 可能受到潛在買家關注，但買方探詢並不代表微軟願意出售，上述估值也不是微軟公布的交易價格。微軟發言人當時回應，Xbox 並未求售。
van Dreunen 另指出，Xbox 執行長 Asha Sharma 成立專責「XP」部門，推動旗下遊戲系列跨足電影、電視等媒體，可能增加 Xbox 對部分買家的吸引力。
在他的分析中，擴大跨媒體業務，有助讓 Xbox 更接近一家擁有多元內容資產的娛樂公司。
不過，這項布局也可以是微軟 (MSFT-US)擴大遊戲 IP 收益的長期經營策略，不能單憑組織調整，就判定公司正在為出售做準備。
目前，Xbox 出售說仍建立在分析師對政策風險、業務表現與潛在買家興趣的綜合推測上。選後政治變局是否足以改變微軟立場，仍須觀察公司後續決策。
paras_en: After the U.S. Democratic Party captured control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, gaming industry analyst Joost van Dreunen believes that political resistance to data‑center construction could prompt Microsoft (MSFT‑US) to reassess its resource allocation and increase the possibility of selling its Xbox business. However, this judgment remains a strategic speculation; Microsoft has previously responded clearly that Xbox is not for sale.

Wccftech reported on Friday the 6th that van Dreunen, co‑founder of market‑research firm SuperData Research and a professor at NYU Stern, suggested in a Substack post that voter dissatisfaction with data‑center expansion, combined with pressure on Xbox revenues, could form the backdrop for Microsoft reevaluating the strategic position of its gaming division.

There is currently no public evidence that Microsoft has initiated a sale process. The key to this analysis is whether policy changes might alter Microsoft’s trade‑offs among its businesses, rather than the election result directly causing an Xbox sale.
Data‑center policy risk rises; analysts focus on resource allocation

Van Dreunen cited a Wall Street Journal report stating that more than 40 U.S. towns and counties put data‑center‑related measures to a voter vote in this election, with at least ten jurisdictions adopting restrictions or outright bans.

He also referenced a nationwide survey of over 79,000 registered voters showing that 56% consider a candidate’s stance on artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers an important factor in their voting decision. Some newly elected Democratic governors have pledged to pause new permits or end tax incentives for new data‑center construction.

If implemented, these measures could affect tech companies’ construction timelines and investment costs. However, local referenda, state policies and federal congressional authority operate at different levels, and Democratic control of Congress does not mean the United States will immediately impose nationwide data‑center restrictions.

Van Dreunen believes Microsoft has made AI infrastructure a major investment focus, and if the expansion environment becomes more complex, management may reassess the strategic value of each business, potentially putting Xbox under review.

Nevertheless, obstacles to data‑center construction could also cause Microsoft to delay spending, which does not necessarily increase the need to sell assets. Thus, there is still no direct causal evidence linking policy risk to an Xbox sale.
Xbox revenue pressure provides context for sale speculation
In addition to policy shifts, the growth performance of the gaming business is another key factor behind van Dreunen’s judgment.

Reports indicate that Xbox revenue has continued to decline; although the rate of decline has narrowed, performance still lags behind some other segments, while Microsoft’s search and advertising businesses are projected to grow revenue by 10% in 2026.

Microsoft has also carried out layoffs and studio closures in its gaming division in recent years. However, these adjustments alone do not prove the company is preparing to sell Xbox, nor can they be directly interpreted as moves to redirect funds to AI.

Revenue decline is just one metric used to assess business value. Whether Microsoft continues to hold Xbox also depends on profitability, cash flow, the company’s gaming intellectual property (IP), and the integration benefits with subscription and cloud services.
Private‑equity buyers reportedly inquire; Microsoft denies any sale intent
The Information reported a few weeks ago that unnamed private‑equity buyers have explored the possibility of acquiring Xbox, valuing the business at roughly $100 billion to $150 billion.

This news shows that Xbox may attract potential buyers, but buyer inquiries do not mean Microsoft is willing to sell, and the cited valuation is not a price disclosed by Microsoft. A Microsoft spokesperson at the time responded that Xbox is not for sale.

Van Dreunen also noted that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has created a dedicated “XP” division to push Xbox game franchises into movies, television and other media, which could increase Xbox’s appeal to certain buyers.
In his analysis, expanding cross‑media activities helps position Xbox more like an entertainment company with diversified content assets.
However, this initiative could also be part of Microsoft’s (MSFT‑US) long‑term strategy to expand gaming IP revenue, and organizational changes alone do not prove the company is preparing for a sale.

Currently, the talk of an Xbox sale rests on analysts’ combined speculation about policy risk, business performance and potential buyer interest. Whether post‑election political shifts are enough to change Microsoft’s stance will require watching the company’s future decisions.

items.title: 美股收盤／晶片股反彈、那指漲1.1%週線仍連四黑
items.title_en: U.S. Stocks Close: Chip Stocks Rebound, Nasdaq Up 1.1% but Weekly Trend Still Shows Four Consecutive Black Days
paras: 2026年11月07日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 美股週五（6日）收盤漲跌互見，科技股在前一日重挫後反彈，晶片股領漲，帶動那斯達克指數上揚1.1%，標普500指數小幅收紅，道瓊指數則續跌。科技股回升未能扭轉整週頹勢，那指週線仍連續第四週下跌，市場持續評估AI投資前景與利率走向。
那斯達克指數收漲264點，報24,579點，漲幅1.1%；標普500指數上漲23點，收7,377點，漲幅0.32%；道瓊工業指數下跌237點，收51,286點，跌幅0.46%。整週來看，那指下跌3.4%，標普500跌2.7%，道瓊跌0.9%，標普500創一年多來最差單週表現。
半導體類股反彈力道最強，費城半導體指數大漲4.2%。輝達(NVDA-US)上漲2.8%，超微(AMD-US)勁揚11%，記憶體業者Sandisk(SNDK-US)回升近4%。科技股開盤走強後守住多數漲幅，那指盤中一度上漲2%，終場漲幅收斂；標普500各類股則表現分歧，資訊科技領漲，民生消費與醫療保健相對落後。
就業數據強於預期，則使市場提高聯準會升息的押注。美國10月非農就業增幅超過市場預估，失業率降至4.1%，顯示勞動市場仍具韌性。依LSEG數據，交易員預估12月升息的機率由稍早的70%升至78%，利率預期成為科技股反彈之外的另一項焦點。
個股方面，特斯拉(TSLA-US)上漲4.2%，同樣自前一日跌勢中回升。企業軟體業者Atlassian(TEAM-US)公布第一季財報後重挫16%；短租平台Airbnb(ABNB-US)上修2026年全年營收成長預測，股價大漲12%，反映財報與展望仍使個股表現明顯分化。
這波震盪已使那指較一個月前高點回落約10%，進入修正區間，週五反彈仍未收復本週失土。能源股同樣承壓，標普500能源類股指數整週下跌12%，為2025年4月以來最差單週表現。

paras_en: On Friday, November 7, 2026 (reporting by You Analysis/Industry Data Center), U.S. markets closed mixed. After a sharp drop the day before, technology stocks rebounded, led by chip stocks, pushing the Nasdaq index up 1.1%. The S&P 500 edged higher, while the Dow Jones continued to fall. The tech rally was not enough to reverse the week’s overall weakness, and the Nasdaq recorded its fourth straight week of declines as the market kept weighing AI investment prospects against interest‑rate direction.

The Nasdaq finished up 264 points at 24,579, a 1.1% gain; the S&P 500 rose 23 points to 7,377, up 0.32%; and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 237 points to 51,286, down 0.46%. Over the full week the Nasdaq slipped 3.4%, the S&P 500 fell 2.7%, and the Dow dropped 0.9%, with the S&P 500 delivering its worst weekly performance in more than a year.

Semiconductor stocks led the rebound, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumping 4.2%. Nvidia (NVDA-US) rose 2.8%, AMD (AMD-US) surged 11%, and memory‑chip maker SanDisk (SNDK-US) recovered nearly 4%. After a strong opening, tech stocks held most of their gains; the Nasdaq was up about 2% mid‑session before narrowing its advance at the close. S&P 500 sectors diverged, with information technology leading gains while consumer staples and health care lagged.

Better‑than‑expected employment data lifted bets on further Fed rate hikes. October non‑farm payrolls exceeded forecasts and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, indicating a still‑resilient labor market. LSEG data show traders now see a 78% probability of a December rate increase, up from 70% earlier, making rate expectations another focal point beyond the tech rebound.

On the stock‑specific front, Tesla (TSLA-US) climbed 4.2%, rebounding from the prior day’s decline. Enterprise‑software firm Atlassian (TEAM-US) saw its shares plunge 16% after releasing its Q1 earnings. Short‑term rental platform Airbnb (ABNB-US) lifted its 2026 full‑year revenue growth outlook, sending the stock up 12% and highlighting the stark performance split among individual equities.

The recent volatility has pulled the Nasdaq about 10% lower from its peak a month ago, placing it in correction territory, and Friday’s bounce did not recover the losses incurred earlier in the week. Energy stocks also felt pressure, with the S&P 500 energy sector index down 12% for the week, marking its worst weekly performance since April 2025.

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉強勁非農撐起美元 周線收紅
items.title_en: <New York FX Market> Strong Nonfarm Payrolls Boost Dollar, Weekly Chart Closes Red
paras: 美元對主要貨幣周五(6日)勁揚，創下近五個月來最大單日漲幅，主因是美國非農就業比意料中強勁，鞏固了聯準會(Fed)下個月升息預期。
追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣走勢的ICE美元指數(DXY)勁揚0.77%，報102.26，創6月17日以來最大漲幅。
歐元兌美元挫跌0.67%，報1.11437美元，創10月1日以來最大單日跌幅。
美元本周上揚0.3%。歐元則下跌0.1%，連續第三周收黑。
美國勞工部公布，10月非農就業人口增加16.5萬人，遠高於經濟學家預估的6.5萬人，9月新增就業人口則上修至6萬人。失業率降至4.1%。
這份報告讓Fed有更大空間繼續升息。根據芝商所(CME)FedWatch工具，報告公布後，市場對12月會議至少升息1碼(25個基點)的預期機率回升至近80%。
美股周四重挫，市場一度預期Fed 下個月升息的機率降至約67%。標普500指數市值蒸發約3兆美元，那斯達克指數則創下19個月來最大單日百分比跌幅。市場擔憂，美國期中選舉後，政府可能對人工智慧(AI)產業建置祭出更嚴格監管，進而拖累經濟成長。
多名議員、國會幕僚及倡議人士表示，民主黨計劃在明年1月掌控美國國會後，推出大量針對AI系統及資料中心發展的新法案。

就業數據公布後市場動態轉變

在就業數據公布前，AI類股賣壓蔓延全球，帶動避險需求，美元已經走高。不過，美股在周五開盤時已趨於穩定，那斯達克指數反彈，終場上漲0.3%。
就業報告公布後，美國公債殖利率走高，10年期公債殖利率上升1.6個基點至4.85%，2年期公債殖利率則上升4.1個基點至4.52%。
Moneycorp交易與結構性商品主管Eugene Epstein說：「這又回到老問題：在任何特定時刻，美元究竟是受到避險需求帶動，還是受到利率差異影響？有時候是其中一種因素，有時候則是另一種，而且兩者可能完全背道而馳，這種情況其實不太合乎理性。」
他表示：「現在市場逐漸塵埃落定，開始消化未來兩年的新常態。我認為，接下來各項資產之間的相關性應該會開始變得更加合理。」

各國央行官員聚焦通膨問題

Fed官員周五的談話，也支持市場對升息的預期。紐約聯邦準備銀行總裁威廉斯(John Williams)周五表示，儘管接連遭遇衝擊，美國經濟成長仍展現出顯著韌性，但通膨水準依然過高，必須讓通膨率回到2%。
另外，聖路易聯邦準備銀行總裁穆薩列姆(Alberto Musalem)表示，在他與所轄中西部地區企業的談話中，通膨仍是最受關注的議題之一。
舊金山聯邦準備銀行總裁戴莉(Mary Daly)則表示，即使科技股出現「令人痛苦」的拋售潮，Fed可能仍需要進一步升息。
英鎊重挫0.71%，報1.3355美元，創下9月23日以來最大單日跌幅。英鎊周四才因英格蘭銀行(BOE，央行)三年多來首度升息，一度攀抵逾七周高點，如今漲勢回吐。
英鎊本周下跌近0.3%，終止連續三周上漲的走勢，是三周以來周線首度收黑。
日元兌美元貶值0.47%，報158.430日元。日本首相高市早苗公布一項計畫，擬運用日本銀行(BOJ，央行)出售ETF所得，為投資計畫提供資金。
日銀總裁植田和男表示，央行預期潛在通膨率將維持在2%目標附近，但也承認通膨存在「一些上行風險」。
日元本周貶值近0.6%，創下9月18日為止一周以來最大單周百分比跌幅，當時貶值幅度超過2%。

paras_en: The dollar surged against major currencies on Friday (the 6th), posting its biggest single‑day gain in nearly five months, driven by U.S. non‑farm payrolls that came in stronger than expected and reinforcing expectations of a Fed rate hike next month.
The ICE Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, jumped 0.77% to 102.26, its largest rise since June 17.
The euro fell 0.67% against the dollar to $1.11437, marking its biggest single‑day drop since October 1.
The dollar rose 0.3% this week, while the euro slipped 0.1%, posting a third consecutive week of losses.

The U.S. Labor Department reported that non‑farm employment increased by 165,000 in October, far above economists’ forecast of 65,000, and September’s figure was revised up to 60,000. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1%.

The report gives the Fed more room to keep raising rates. According to CME’s FedWatch tool, after the release the market’s probability of at least a 25‑basis‑point hike at the December meeting rose to near 80%.

U.S. equities slumped heavily on Thursday, with the market at one point expecting the Fed’s hike probability to fall to about 67%. The S&P 500 lost roughly $3 trillion in market cap and the Nasdaq posted its biggest single‑day percentage drop in 19 months. Investors worry that after the mid‑term elections the government may impose stricter AI regulations, which could weigh on growth.

Several lawmakers, congressional staffers and advocates said Democrats plan to roll out a wave of new legislation targeting AI systems and data‑center development after they take control of Congress in January next year.

Market dynamics shifted after the jobs data were released. Before the report, AI‑related stocks were under sell pressure worldwide, driving safe‑haven demand and lifting the dollar. However, U.S. equities steadied by Friday’s open and the Nasdaq rebounded, ending the session up 0.3%.
Following the jobs report, U.S. Treasury yields rose, with the 10‑year yield up 1.6 basis points to 4.85% and the two‑year yield up 4.1 basis points to 4.52%.

Eugene Epstein, head of trading and structured products at Moneycorp, said: “This brings us back to the old question: at any given moment, is the dollar being driven by safe‑haven demand or by interest‑rate differentials? Sometimes it’s one, sometimes the other, and they can even move in opposite directions, which isn’t very rational.”
He added: “The market is now gradually settling and beginning to digest the new normal for the next two years. I think the correlations among assets will start to look more sensible.”

Central‑bank officials around the world focused on inflation. Fed officials’ remarks on Friday also supported market expectations for a rate hike. New York Fed President John Williams said that despite a series of shocks, the U.S. economy remains remarkably resilient, but inflation is still too high and must be brought back to 2%.
In addition, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said that in conversations with businesses in his Mid‑West district, inflation remains one of the top concerns.
San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly noted that even though tech stocks have experienced a “painful” sell‑off, the Fed may still need to raise rates further.

The pound fell 0.71% to $1.3355, its biggest single‑day drop since September 23. The pound had risen on Thursday after the Bank of England’s first rate hike in over three years, reaching a seven‑week high before giving back the gains.
The pound is down about 0.3% this week, ending three weeks of gains and posting its first weekly loss in three weeks.
The yen weakened 0.47% against the dollar to ¥158.43. Japanese Prime Minister Kishida announced a plan to use proceeds from the Bank of Japan’s ETF sales to fund an investment program.
BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said the central bank expects potential inflation to stay near its 2% target, but acknowledged there are “some upside risks” to inflation.
The yen has depreciated nearly 0.6% this week, marking its biggest weekly percentage drop since the week ending September 18, when it fell more than 2%.
